correctness.rationale: The Gaussian Schur-complement risk is exact. Cauchy–Schwarz minimizes the jointly allocated independent measurement noise as squared total variation of signed quadrature weights. Exponential covariance has a tridiagonal Stieltjes precision matrix; integrated Markov interpolation is strictly positive, making all active weights positive. At an optimum endpoint shifts strictly decrease error, and splitting an atom yields a strict first-order improvement, so all sensors are distinct and interior. Residual-potential derivative jumps and its inhomogeneous Helmholtz ODE force equal weights/interior gaps/symmetric margins; the remaining scalar equation has a strictly monotone unique root. The spacing threshold follows algebraically. Standalone verifier reports 656 formula/design checks plus 4788 finite competitor comparisons, corroborating but not replacing the proof.

value.rationale: This solves the natural exact finite-n joint sampling/measurement-resource design for a stationary Markov Gaussian integrand, without fixing either node positions or per-node noise. It adds an all-n positive-weights classification, proof of nonredundancy of each sensor, exact risk, and a dimensionless P=n grid transition independent of covariance scale, relevant to budgeting repeated measurements and noisy Gaussian-process numerical integration. The special two-sensor or noiseless cases do not resolve the arbitrary-n resource allocation.
